newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea First shareholders file law suit.
newsitem.headline: Korea First shareholders file law suit.

text.p: Minority shareholders of the Korea First Bank have filed a law suit against four former bank executives in connection with loans to failed Hanbo Steel Co, a bank spokesman said on Wednesday.

The suit, filed by a group of 53 shareholders, alleged former presidents Sheen Kwang-shik and Rhee Chul-soo, and two other executives were responsible for the bank's non-performing loans of 1.07 trillion won to the steelmaker, he said.
The spokesman said the shareholders demanded 10 billion won as an indemnity to the bank.
Korea First Bank is Hanbo's prime creditor.
The shareholders, quoted by the spokesman, said the four executives played a leading role in the bank's decision to extend the loans without proper credit analysis.

Hanbo Steel collapsed in January after piling up $5.8 billion in debts. Hanbo officials had said the company's heavy investment in expanding a steel mill in Tangjin, south of Seoul, led to its collapse.

"It's not quite right to say bank presidents should assume all responsibilities for bank loans," the spokesman said. "It has not yet been determined if the loans to Hanbo actually constituted the bank's bad loans."
